title: Dominion Dynamics and Telesat to develop ruggedized antennas to connect with Telesat Lightspeed | Telesat
body_markdown:
*Companies partnering on project to engineer Canadian-made technology that provides operators with access to a secure, Canadian-controlled network*


OTTAWA, ON — November 19, 2026 — Dominion Dynamics, an Ottawa-based defence technology company, and Telesat LEO ULC (Telesat LEO), a subsidiary of Telesat Corporation (Nasdaq and TSX: TSAT), one of the world’s largest satellite operators, have teamed up to develop ruggedized antennas intended to securely connect dismounted operators and uncrewed military platforms to the Telesat Lightspeed low Earth orbit (LEO) constellation.


“A soldier on patrol in Canada’s most remote regions and the uncrewed platforms they use should be connected to a Canadian network through equipment built here at home,” said Mitch Carkner, Chief Operating Officer at Dominion Dynamics. “While the CAF are the first intended users, the same technology could also serve the Canadian Rangers, the Canadian Coast Guard, the Royal Canadian Mounted Police and emergency management in the High North.”


The $2.2-million project includes a contribution to Dominion Dynamics from the National Research Council’s Industrial Research Assistance Program and is intended to provide operators in the Arctic with a Canadian-controlled communications link to command centres across the country.


“Through investments in research and development, the Government of Canada is helping Canadian companies grow, innovate and develop technologies that strengthen Canada’s economy and strategic capabilities. Congratulations to Dominion Dynamics and Telesat on this exciting collaboration,” said Hon. Mélanie Joly, Minister of Industry and Minister responsible for Canada Economic Development for Quebec Regions. “By developing advanced communications technologies here in Canada, these companies are helping build solutions for remote and northern environments while supporting Canadian innovation and creating new opportunities for growth.”


Following this initial phase, Dominion intends to design and manufacture two user terminal prototypes: a compact unit light enough for a dismounted soldier to carry and a larger terminal built for uncrewed systems, including Dominion Scout. As Canada’s first sovereign Autonomous Collaborative Platform, Scout is an uncrewed combat aircraft being developed to extend the reach of Canada’s future fighter fleet.


The terminals are being designed with the Canadian Armed Forces (CAF) in mind as the first potential customer. They are intended to operate in Arctic and expeditionary conditions, run on tactical power, and use open interfaces for integration with existing hardware. The prototypes are expected to undergo both cold-weather field trials, including service connectivity testing with Telesat Lightspeed.


“Kanata and Ottawa are home to some of Canada’s most innovative technology and defence companies, and this partnership between Dominion Dynamics and Telesat demonstrates the strength of that ecosystem,” said Hon. Jenna Sudds, Member of Parliament for Kanata. “By bringing together local expertise to develop homegrown technologies for our Armed Forces, these companies are helping strengthen Canada’s national security, sovereignty and defence capabilities. This is exactly the kind of innovation and collaboration we need to build Canada strong.”


Dominion Dynamics will lead the project as Prime contractor, with Telesat LEO acting as subcontractor. Together, the companies aim to deliver sovereign capability with intellectual property created and maintained in Canada.


“This is a great example of two Canadian companies combining their expertise in support of our national sovereignty,” said Stephen Hampton, Vice President, Canada and Sovereign Initiatives at Telesat. “The collaboration reflects the growing strength of Canada’s defence industrial base, and we look forward to working with Dominion to develop solutions that leverage the advanced capabilities we will integrate into the Telesat Lightspeed network.”


Telesat Lightspeed is expected to enter high-latitude commercial service around the end of Q1 2028.
